judgment.observations: The reconstruction captures the long workshop bench, bright windows, large spoked wheel, central anvil, foreground lathe, open drawer and pale bin. Framing is tighter and more frontal: the foreground machine extends beyond the right edge, and less floor and left-side workshop are visible. The reference has much denser clutter, including window-sill containers, hand tools, hanging implements, machinery and under-bench storage; many are omitted or simplified. The anvil and machines have different silhouettes and proportions, with blockier bodies and cleaner spacing. The drawer projects into the aisle in both images, but its contents and surrounding supports differ. Materials are substantially cleaner and flatter: pale wood and uniform gray metal replace dark worn timber, rust, grime and varied metallic surfaces. The floor lacks the reference’s prominent plank detail, and visible render noise obscures fine surfaces.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The reconstruction appears to place the machines along a straighter, more uniform bench, while the reference suggests more varied offsets and heights; perspective could account for some of this difference. Machine feet appear to meet the countertop, but simplified forms and weak contact shadows make attachment and support uncertain. The drawer appears farther extended and the anvil more elevated relative to nearby equipment, though these are image-based depth impressions rather than verified geometry.
